title: Square of a Number
description:
A function packs a small job under a name so you can reuse it.
Define `int square(int n)` that returns `n * n`, and call it from `main`.

Input: one integer `n`.
Output: the square of `n` on one line.

title: Larger of Two Numbers
description:
Define `int maxOf(int a, int b)` that returns the larger of its two parameters.

Input: two integers `a` and `b` separated by a space.
Output: the larger value on one line.

title: Print a Row of Stars
description:
A `void` function does work but returns nothing.
Define `void printStars(int n)` that prints `n` asterisks followed by a newline.

Input: one integer `n`.
Output: a single line with `n` stars.

title: Even or Odd Function
description:
Define `int isEven(int n)` that returns 1 if `n` is even and 0 otherwise. Remember negative numbers: use `n % 2 == 0`.

Input: one integer `n`.
Output: `Even` if isEven returns 1, otherwise `Odd`.

title: Sum from 1 to N
description:
Define `long long sumTo(int n)` that returns 1 + 2 + ... + n using a loop. For `n = 0` the sum is 0.

Input: one integer `n`.
Output: the sum on one line.

title: Factorial Function
description:
The factorial of n is 1 * 2 * ... * n, and 0! = 1.
Define `long long factorial(int n)` using a loop.

Input: one integer `n`.
Output: n! on one line.

title: Sum of an Array
description:
Arrays are passed to functions together with their size.
Define `int arraySum(int arr[], int n)` returning the sum of the first `n` elements.

Input: first `n`, then `n` integers.
Output: their sum on one line.

title: Absolute Value
description:
Define `int absolute(int n)` that returns `n` if it is non-negative, otherwise `-n`. Do not use the library `abs`.

Input: one integer `n`.
Output: the absolute value.

title: Count the Digits
description:
Define `int countDigits(int n)` that returns how many digits the non-negative number `n` has. The number 0 has 1 digit.
Hint: keep dividing by 10.

Input: one integer `n`.
Output: the digit count.

title: Prime Checker
description:
A prime is a number greater than 1 with no divisors other than 1 and itself.
Define `int isPrime(int n)` returning 1 for prime, else 0.

Input: one integer `n`.
Output: `Prime` or `Not Prime`.

title: GCD and LCM
description:
Define `int gcd(int a, int b)` (Euclid: repeat `a, b = b, a % b` until b is 0) and `long long lcm(int a, int b)` which uses gcd (lcm = a / gcd * b).

Input: two positive integers `a` and `b`.
Output: gcd and lcm separated by a single space.

title: Power Function
description:
Define `long long power(int base, int exp)` that returns base raised to exp using a loop (no `pow`). Anything to the power 0 is 1.

Input: `base` and `exp` separated by a space.
Output: the result.
constraints: The result fits in long long

title: Static Call Counter
description:
A `static` local variable keeps its value between calls.
Define `int nextId(void)` that holds `static int id = 0;`, increments it, and returns it. Call it `n` times.

Input: one integer `n`.
Output: the returned values, one per line (1 to n).

title: Reverse an Array in Place
description:
Arrays passed to functions are shared with the caller, so changes persist.
Define `void reverseArray(int arr[], int n)` that reverses the array in place by swapping ends.

Input: `n`, then `n` integers.
Output: the reversed array on one line, separated by single spaces.

title: Function Composition
description:
Define `long long f(long long x)` returning `2*x + 1`, and `long long g(long long x)` returning `x*x`. Then compute the compositions g(f(x)) and f(g(x)) by calling one function with the result of the other.

Input: one integer `x`.
Output: g(f(x)) and f(g(x)) separated by a single space.

title: Primes in a Range
description:
Write a helper `int isPrime(int n)` and a function `int countPrimes(int a, int b)` that uses it to count primes in the inclusive range [a, b].

Input: two integers `a` and `b` with a <= b.
Output: the number of primes, then a space, then the sum of those primes.

title: Perfect Numbers up to N
description:
A perfect number equals the sum of its proper divisors (6 = 1+2+3). Define `int isPerfect(int n)` returning 1 or 0, and use it to find all perfect numbers from 1 to `n`.

Input: one integer `n`.
Output: each perfect number on its own line in increasing order, or `None` if there is none.

title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
description:
Define `void mergeSorted(int a[], int n, int b[], int m, int out[])` that merges two ascending arrays into `out` (length n+m), still ascending. Walk both arrays with two indices, always copying the smaller current element; then copy leftovers. Duplicates are kept.

Input: `n` then `n` integers, then `m` then `m` integers (each array already sorted ascending).
Output: the merged array on one line separated by single spaces.

title: Fast Modular Power
description:
Computing base^exp directly overflows, and a plain loop is too slow for huge exponents. Define `long long powMod(long long base, long long exp, long long mod)` using repeated squaring: while exp > 0, if exp is odd multiply result by base (mod), then square base (mod) and halve exp. Always reduce with `% mod`.

Input: `base`, `exp`, `mod` separated by spaces.
Output: (base^exp) % mod.

title: Matrix Multiplication Function
description:
Define `void multiply(int n, int a[][5], int b[][5], int c[][5])` that stores the product of two n x n matrices in `c`: c[i][j] = sum over k of a[i][k] * b[k][j]. A 2D array parameter must state its column count.

Input: `n`, then matrix A (n rows of n integers), then matrix B.
Output: matrix C, one row per line, values separated by single spaces.
